newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-DAVIES TAKES FIRST-ROUND LEAD IN LPGA CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DAVIES TAKES FIRST-ROUND LEAD IN LPGA CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Defending champion Laura Davies of Britain got off to a solid start, firing a 4-under-par 67 for a one-shot lead after the first round of the $1.2 million LPGA Championship on Thursday.
Davies, who also won this event in 1994, finished strongly with birdies on three of the final five holes and leads Kim Saiki, Barb Mucha, Chris Johnson and Sherri Steinhauer by one stroke.
Nancy Lopez, one of four players who have won this event at least three times, shot a 2-under 69 and is tied for sixth with Pat Hurst, Mitzi Edge, Tina Barrett, Gail Graham and Shelley Hamlin.
Davies, the 1996 LPGA Player of the Year, had six birdies and two bogeys on the Du Pont Country Club course, where she won last year's rain-shortened event by one shot over Julie Piers.

Davies sank a four-foot putt on the par-4 third hole for her first birdie, but returned to even-par by two-putting from eight feet for a bogey at the par-3 eighth. She gained momentum with back-to-back birdies on the ninth and 10th holes before making what she described as her "only mistake of the day" at number 12, where she chipped past the hole for another bogey.

Davies rallied with tap-ins for birdies at the par-4 14th and par-5 16th holes, then rolled in a 12-footer for her sixth birdie at number 17. She maintained sole possession of the lead by saving par at 18.

"I've been playing very well," said Davies. "I just haven't been making the putts. Today, instead of chipping to five feet and missing them, I've been chipping to a foot and tapping them in. That's the only difference.
"I've hit it slightly closer to where I can't miss the putts. I'm actually not surprised, you know, although I'm very pleased."

The 33-year-old Davies has one win this year and is fourth on the LPGA money list with $258,171. She is seeking her fourth major championship after winning the LPGA Championship and the du Maurier Classic last year.

"I don't think of it as being a favourite," Davies said. "I think of it as I'm comfortable on the golf course and I've got so many memories. Every hole, something good's happened to me around this golf course.
"It's difficult not to be happy. And even when I went back to level par, when I bogeyed number eight, I still felt good even though it wasn't the best of starts."
Annika Sorenstam of Sweden, the 1997 money leader and one of two multiple winners on tour this year, had a 1-under 70 and is among 12 golfers who trail Davies by three strokes.
Sorenstam has won twice this year and has been a runner-up three times. She is no stranger to major championship, winning the U.S. Women's Open each of the last two years.
Karrie Webb, second on the money list, is another stroke back after an even-par 71.
Hall of Famer Betsy King, a former champion who won the Dinah Shore at the end of March, struggled to a 5-over 76 Thursday.
Terry-Jo Myers, who last week joined Sorenstam as a multiple winner when she captured the Sara Lee Classic in a playoff, had a 3-over 75.
